## Historical audit: S0298

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/historical_r1_C2_start/development/commons_189918915/1/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines in this file. The supplied observations contain paths, not viewable image pixels.

**Goal versus observation.** The assigned goal was to reconstruct a single indoor photograph with separate meshes and a matching camera. The student interpreted it as a warehouse aisle; that semantic interpretation is not independently verified here (H `model_request`, line 1; H `model_response`, line 3).

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H authored multiple named assets: roof, skylight, lights, racks, pallets, cartons and enclosure. Rack uprights, braces and supports are separate children; goods are positioned by coordinates rather than persistent support bindings. Colored box/rod geometry represents steel, wood, wrapping and cartons; no image texture is used. The code sets camera and area lights (lines 3–4). Naming and hierarchy do not verify physical connections or reference fidelity. |
| First validation and revision | Build and render completed with return code 0; step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10). The next request supplied the reference and render to H (line 11). H **reported**, rather than independently established for this audit, a blank wall, excess opposite rack, wrong convergence and a small dark skylight. It revised camera aim and roll, skylight size/emission and distant rack placement; step 2 executed and rendered successfully (lines 13–14, 16, 18–20). |
| Second review and revision | After receiving the second render (line 21), H reported that the roll tilted the scene in the opposite direction. It reversed the roll from +24° to −24°, moved the far wall, added pallet blocks/openings and a ceiling fitting, and changed colors; this complete program was executed (lines 23–24). Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected (lines 26, 28–30). No subsequent visual review or `DONE` is visible. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** The system instructions supplied inventory, complexity, validation and correction procedures, including world initialization (line 1). The student’s inventory, primitive estimates, post-realization world setup and render-driven revisions are consistent with adoption, although not proof of the source of every choice. No separate teacher diagnosis or intervention is recorded. H independently produced two comparisons and revisions; session records show no observed external tool calls within its model sessions (lines 2, 12, 22). The runner’s Blender executions are separately recorded.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **technical build/render success**, not verified reconstruction success or demonstrated partial geometric correctness. Multiple objects and intended parts are evidenced by code, but actual visible coverage, texture appearance, connections, object pose, lighting, framing and improvement after the last roll reversal cannot be checked without the images. No algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption is recorded. The student’s camera diagnosis remains a hypothesis, not proof of a unique cause.

**Lessons.** Transferable: distinguish successful rendering from image matching, and compare a full render before revising. Task-specific: the warehouse inventory, skylight and roll corrections are the student’s scene hypotheses, not generally validated facts.
